Which era
are you?

Twelve questions. Your answers are encrypted on this computer before they're sent for scoring, scored while they're still encrypted, and unlocked back on this computer. The scoring service only ever gets them encrypted.

How can it score answers it can't read?

This quiz uses fully homomorphic encryption (FHE). Picture a locked glass box with gloves built into the side. Anyone can reach in through the gloves and rearrange what's inside, but only the person with the key can open the lid.

Your answers go into the box on this computer. The scoring service reaches in through the gloves, runs the math that compares you with each era, and sends the box back still locked. This computer opens it. The scoring service only ever holds the locked box, never your answers, your scores, or your era.

Locked on this computer

          
Your 12 answers became 8 numbers, one per trait. The quiz's local helper program encrypted them on this computer with a public key. The matching secret key is never sent to the scoring service.

          
See the math
            
Your answers, turned into 8 trait numbers and scaled to length 1. Each era is 8 numbers too. Your score for an era is how closely the two sets point the same way (cosine similarity), shown as 50 × (1 + score).
